title: Jude and the Wolf Again
premise: Cyrus Ishikawa, a bone-carver who hears the dead and keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent years erasing themself from every record—including the guild's—under the childhood name Jude. When a dying courier presses them a map to a door out of Vessany, a country that was annexed and struck from all maps a generation ago, Cyrus learns they are the last registered heir of Vessany's vanished royal line—and that the guild intends to trade that inheritance to the annexing empire. Hunted by the guild's enforcer, a wolf-shaped debt-collector called the Hound who once belonged to Cyrus's grandmother, Cyrus must reach the door before the ledger that defines Vessany's existence is burned at the equinox. In the end, Cyrus chooses not to escape through the door but to claim the inheritance, rewriting the ledger so Vessany exists again in memory if not on maps—and freeing the Hound, who is revealed to be their grandmother's bound spirit, from the guild's service.
about_author: Mara Thackeray is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing the paper trails of dissolved nations before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about bureaucracy, grief, and the stubborn persistence of small countries, and lives near a border that has changed hands four times.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the guild's counting house, Cyrus carves a bone whistle for a client's dead mother while quietly erasing another entry of themself from the master ledger. The chapter establishes the guild's trade in impossible things and Cyrus's careful invisibility. Emotional beat: the ache of a self kept deliberately blank, and the first whisper of the dead warning that someone is coming.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Loading Door
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. A courier, half-dead from running, collapses at the guild's loading door and presses a folded map into Cyrus's hands, whispering that the door out of Vessany opens at equinox and that 'the heir must sign.' The guild's provost arrives too late to save him. Emotional beat: terror and unwilling responsibility; Cyrus realizes the dead man's voice now lives in the map's vellum.

chapters.title: What the Guild Cannot Price
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The provost discovers the map and reveals, gently and terribly, that Cyrus's erased entries were never hidden—the guild has always known Cyrus is Vessany's last heir, an asset waiting to appreciate. The empire's buyers are already en route. Emotional beat: betrayal; invisibility was never protection, only patience on the guild's part.

chapters.title: The Hound at the Threshold
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, with interludes in the Hound's. The guild unleashes the Hound, a wolf-shaped debt-collector, to retrieve the map. Cyrus flees into the flooded lower city, guided by the dead courier's voice. In the Hound's interlude, something in the wolf recognizes Cyrus's face and hesitates. Emotional beat: pursuit, and the first crack in the hunter's certainty.

chapters.title: Country of Ash and Registry
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In the ruins of the old Vessany archive, the dead of the annexation crowd around Cyrus, each demanding to be remembered, each a name the empire struck from record. Cyrus learns the map leads to the Door of Return, but it requires a signature in royal blood. Emotional beat: grief as a physical weight; the dead are not menacing, just unbearably hopeful.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Bone Knife
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Hiding in a bone-carver's abandoned workshop, Cyrus finds their grandmother's tools and a carved wolf figurine matching the Hound exactly—evidence she bound a guardian spirit before her death, and the guild seized it. The Hound corners Cyrus here but cannot strike, drawn by the figurine. Emotional beat: inheritance reframed—not land or title, but a debt of love the guild has been collecting on.

chapters.title: Equinox Eve
chapters.summary: Alternating Cyrus and the Hound's POV. The guild burns the archive to erase the dead's testimony; the Hound, ordered to finish Cyrus, instead turns on its handlers and is punished by its binding-collar. Cyrus, watching from the hills, understands the price of the Door: a signature freely given, which the guild will force from them at the exchange. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. At the Door of Return, the guild offers Cyrus to the empire's buyers: sign, and live comfortably as a puppet heir legitimizing the annexation; refuse, and the ledger burns with Vessany's existence inside it. The Hound, collar cracking, drags itself to stand between them. Emotional beat: the trap closing, and Cyrus realizing every offered choice is a cage.

chapters.title: Jude Signs
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Climax. Cyrus signs—not the empire's contract, but the old royal ledger of Vessany itself, claiming the inheritance and seizing authority over every debt the guild holds, including the Hound's binding. The guild's provost is undone by her own accounting; the Door of Return opens not out of the country, but into its remembered heart. Emotional beat: power taken and immediately feared for what it might make of its holder.

chapters.title: A Wolf Unbound
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Resolution. Cyrus frees the Hound, who takes human shape at last: their grandmother, returned to finish dying in peace, leaving Cyrus the bone knife and a warning about ledgers that hold nations. Cyrus reopens the guild's books under new rules—every erased name restored, every impossible thing fairly traded. Emotional beat: belonging chosen at last, and the quiet terror of holding power without being corrupted by it—yet.
